name: Macondo
description: A star 29 parsecs away, 84% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 52521: radius 0.838 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.387 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 52521: effective temperature 4976 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.026)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 52521: distance 28.636 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 29 parsecs away, 84% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 0.387 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,976 K, so 0.838 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 52521: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 93083
quotes.card: HD 93083 is an orange-hued star in the southern constellation of Antlia.
quotes.introduction: It has the proper name Macondo, after the mythical village of the novel One Hundred Years of Solitude.
